title: DemoGrasp: Universal Dexterous Grasping from a Single Demonstration
claim: One simple method from a single example yields universal, state-of-the-art performance across embodiments, datasets, and real-world conditions.
layout: 3 columns, center-out hub; sim and bar chart left, real-world right
description: A wide banner figure with a warm orange-to-blue gradient background. The center column stacks a rendered robot hand labeled 'A Single Demonstration', two chevron arrows around the bold 'DemoGrasp' title, and a mosaic of colorful 3D object models labeled 'Universal Dexterous Grasping'. The left column has a 4x6 grid of simulation renders. Columns are labeled Shadow, Allegro, Inspire, Schunk, DClaw and Panda, with the caption 'Extend to Various Embodiments and Datasets'. Under it is a grouped bar chart of success rates on DexGraspNet. DemoGrasp bars are hatched and lead UniGraspTransformer, UniDexGrasp++ and UniDexGrasp. The right column has a 3x6 photo grid of real-world grasps captioned '87% Success Rate on 110 Real-World Objects'. Below are smaller photo panels for small and thin objects, language-guided cluttered grasp, closed-loop sim-to-real with various cameras, and robustness to background and lighting changes. The eye goes first to the central DemoGrasp title.
caption: DemoGrasp uses a single demonstration trajectory to learn universal dexterous grasping, formulating each grasping trial as a demonstration-editing process. For each trial, the Demo Editor policy takes observations at the first timestep and outputs an end-effector transformation and a delta hand pose. The actions in the demonstration are then transformed accordingly and applied in the simulator. The policy is trained using RL across diverse objects, optimizing a simple reward consisting of binary success and a collision penalty. A flow-matching policy is trained on successful rollouts with rendered images to enable sim-to-real transfer.
abstract: Universal grasping with multi-fingered dexterous hands is a fundamental challenge in robotic manipulation. While recent approaches successfully learn closed-loop grasping policies using reinforcement learning (RL), the inherent difficulty of high-dimensional, long-horizon exploration necessitates complex reward and curriculum design, often resulting in suboptimal solutions across diverse objects. We propose DemoGrasp, a simple yet effective method for learning universal dexterous grasping. We start from a single successful demonstration trajectory of grasping a specific object and adapt to novel objects and poses by editing the robot actions in this trajectory: changing the wrist pose determines where to grasp, and changing the hand joint angles determines how to grasp. We formulate this trajectory editing as a single-step Markov Decision Process (MDP) and use RL to optimize a universal policy across hundreds of objects in parallel in simulation, with a simple reward consisting of a binary success term and a robot-table collision penalty. In simulation, DemoGrasp achieves a 95% success rate on DexGraspNet objects using the Shadow Hand, outperforming previous state-of-the-art methods. It also shows strong transferability, achieving an average success rate of 84.6% across diverse dexterous hand embodiments on six unseen object datasets, while being trained on only 175 objects. Through vision-based imitation learning, our policy successfully grasps 110 unseen real-world objects, including small, thin items. It generalizes to spatial, background, and lighting changes, supports both RGB and depth inputs, and extends to language-guided grasping in cluttered scenes.
